name: – Mohammed Chahim – Commission proposal and amendment
title: SECOND REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1252
part_text:
The report sets out Parliament's position on changing the EU's 2024 law on critical raw materials — metals and minerals Europe needs for clean energy, digital technology and defence. It adds new rules on company risk checks, recycling labels and stockpiles, and it creates a new EU agency, the European Critical Raw Materials Centre, to buy, store and finance these materials. Parliament now negotiates the final text with EU governments.

- **What changes:** A new EU agency will stockpile and jointly buy critical raw materials; companies face stricter supply risk checks.
- **Who it affects:** Large manufacturers using these materials, recyclers, and EU governments.
- **What happens next:** Parliament and EU governments negotiate the final law; the agency's seat is decided by 2028.
